name: Prefix sums + hash
summary: Answer 'sum of any range' instantly by storing running totals; count ranges with a target sum using a hash map.

name: Monotonic stack
summary: For every element, find the nearest bigger (or smaller) one to its left or right, all in a single pass.

name: Two pointers on sorted data
summary: Find a pair (or shrink a range) in sorted data by walking one pointer from each end toward the middle.

name: Sliding window
summary: Find the longest or shortest stretch of consecutive elements that obeys a rule, by growing the right edge and shrinking the left.

name: Binary search on the answer
summary: When you can't compute the answer but can check 'is X good enough?', binary-search over X itself.

name: BFS shortest path
summary: Fewest steps from a start to a target when every step costs the same: explore in rings, first arrival wins.

name: DFS + backtracking
summary: List every valid combination by making one choice at a time, going deeper, and undoing the choice on the way back.

name: Union-find
summary: Keep track of which items belong to the same group while groups keep merging; 'are these two connected?' in near O(1).

name: Topological sort
summary: Put tasks in an order that respects 'A before B' rules, and spot when the rules contradict each other (a cycle).

name: Dijkstra
summary: Cheapest route between points when each road has its own positive cost: always extend the cheapest known route next.

name: Heap / top-k
summary: Keep only the k best things you've seen so far (or always grab the smallest of many streams) with a priority queue.

name: Intervals
summary: Sort time ranges by start, then sweep left to right merging, counting overlaps, or picking non-overlapping ones.

name: 1-D DP
summary: Solve 'best answer for the first i elements' using the answers for slightly shorter prefixes, filling a table left to right.

name: Grid / 2-D DP
summary: Two-dimensional table: the answer for cell (i, j) comes from its neighbours — grids, or two strings compared prefix by prefix.

name: Knapsack-style DP
summary: Pick items under a limit (weight, budget, target sum): a table over 'how much capacity is left' tells you what is reachable.

name: DP on intervals
summary: Best way to process a range [l, r] by choosing which element is handled last, then solving the two sides.

name: Bitmask DP
summary: When n ≤ ~20, represent 'which items are used so far' as bits of an integer and DP over all 2^n subsets.

name: Trie
summary: A tree of letters so that looking up words, prefixes or 'does any word start with…' is proportional to word length, not dictionary size.

name: Linked list pointers
summary: Slow/fast pointers to find middles and cycles, in-place reversal, and a dummy head so the first node is never a special case.

name: Trees: recursion that returns
summary: Each recursive call returns a tiny summary of its subtree (height, sum, best path); the parent combines the children's summaries.

name: Greedy + sort
summary: Sort by the right key, then take the locally best choice every time; justify it by showing swapping never helps.

name: Fenwick / segment tree
summary: Range queries mixed with updates in O(log n); also the standard tool for 'count smaller elements after me'.

name: Divide and conquer
summary: Split in half, solve each half, then count the pairs that straddle the middle during the merge (like merge sort).

name: Design / hashing
summary: Build data structures with O(1) operations by pairing a hash map with an array or a doubly linked list (LRU, O(1) getRandom).

name: Math / counting
summary: Closed-form formulas, modular arithmetic, parity and pigeonhole arguments that replace a loop with a calculation.
